scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.

xref.title: The Residents (Shreveport LA, 1969) – No Known Members; Hardy W. Fox Died 2018 Listed as Co-Founder; George Harrison and Claypool Denied
xref.body: The Residents are an art collective that originated in Shreveport, Louisiana in 1969. By 1971 they were performing in San Francisco. They have never shown their faces or listed any band members — their only point of contact is a company called Cryptic Music. When their debut album Meet the Residents was released in 1974 (parodying the Beatles' Meet the Beatles), some fans believed they were actually the Beatles in disguise. Hardy W. Fox — who claimed to have been a Resident — died in 2018 with his obituary listing him as co-founder and primary songwriter. Other names tied to the band include Homer Cook (unconfirmed), Jay Clem (maybe), and "Charles Boebuck" (apparently a pseudonym for Fox). Contrary to rumors, George Harrison, Les Claypool of Primus, and no member of Devo has ever been in the band. "I can tell you, though, contrary to rumors, George Harrison less clay pool of primus, and no one from Devo has ever been in the residence."

xref.title: Instrument Variety
xref.body: Les Claypool utilizes a range of instruments, including standard four-string basses, six-string basses when needed, and various stand-up basses. "Some of his guitars have the standard four strings. He also plays a six string bass when the knee derises, or if necessary, any variety of stand-up basses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Les Claypool Comparison
xref.body: Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers was used as a point of comparison for Les Claypool's bass playing style, crossed with Geddy Lee of Rush. "If you want to compare Les to anyone, do it with Getty Lee of Rush, crossed with flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

xref.title: Les Claypool – Rejected by Metallica for Being "Too Good"
xref.body: Les Claypool is known for an unmatched and versatile attack on the bass, combining funk, slapping, strumming, and effects — often while singing simultaneously. A widely told anecdote holds that he was deemed "too good" when he auditioned for Metallica. "Combines funk, slapping, strumming, and effects use, with a myth that he was 'too good' for Metallica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Les Claypool's Bass-Driven Style
xref.body: Primus's music, a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, is primarily built around the distinctive bass grooves of singer and bass player Les Claypool. Claypool is described as an inventive player, unafraid to push boundaries, with a style comparable to Geddy Lee of Rush crossed with Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "Primus, experiments with a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, all built around singer and bass player Les Claypool's grooves. Great player, very inventive, never afraid to push boundaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Metallica Bassist Audition Anecdote
xref.body: There is a story that Les Claypool was offered the position of bassist in Metallica after Cliff Burton's death, but he did not get the job because, as quoted, "he was too good." "Now, there's a story that says he was offered the job of bassist in Metallica after the death of Cliff Burton, but he didn't get the job because, and this is a quote, he was too good."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Simultaneous Vocals and Bass
xref.body: Live, Les Claypool performs his complex bass techniques while also singing lead vocals. "And live, he does all this while singing lead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unconventional Bass Techniques
xref.body: Les Claypool is known for his unique and aggressive approach to the bass, which includes rocking out, getting super funky, strumming, slapping, and tapping the strings with his fingers. "He can rock out, he can get super funky, he strums the strings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Use of Whammy Bar and Effects
xref.body: Some of Les Claypool's basses are equipped with a whammy bar, allowing him to bend notes in unusual ways. He also processes his notes through a series of processors and distortion pedals to achieve diverse sounds. "Some of his guitars have a whammy bar, which is really weird, so he can bend notes in unusual ways."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
